title: 6 Techniques to Master Self Discipline | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
Motivation starts things. Discipline finishes them.

This video breaks down why self-discipline is the real driver behind progress — not intensity, not inspiration, and not perfect conditions. Results come from small commitments kept consistently, especially when it’s uncomfortable and inconvenient.

Discipline isn’t punishment. It’s alignment.

What you’ll learn in this video:
-How small commitments compound into real momentum
-Why consistency beats perfection every time
-Using prioritization to stop leaking time and energy
-Turning daily actions into automatic habits
-Delaying short-term comfort for long-term payoff

Discipline is the system that turns intention into execution. When habits are installed, progress no longer depends on mood or motivation. The work gets done because it’s who you are — not because you feel like it.

This video is for anyone who feels stuck, overwhelmed, or inconsistent and wants a clear framework for moving forward without burning out. Progress doesn’t require drastic change — it requires reliable action.

When discipline is in place, success becomes predictable.

This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

description:

At one point or another, we’ve all felt stuck in a rut with feelings of laziness and fear. During these times it can be really hard to take a step back and wonder what’s happening in the body, as opposed to just the mind, but it’s the link between the two that can push us through it.  

Neurotransmitters have some incredible power over how we function. Dopamine is responsible for craving, motivation, and pursuit. Adrenaline relates to agitation and endurance. Serotonin helps us be grateful and feel good about what we have. And acetylcholine can help us focus. This is just a snapshot of the chemical symphony happening in our bodies all the time, and we can actually leverage these inner reactions to better understand the way we react to the world around us and make positive changes. 

Today on The Dhru Purohit Podcast, Dhru talks to Dr. Andrew Huberman about opening the window into our neurochemistry, training the nervous system, and confronting our inner real estate. 

Dr. Andrew Huberman is a neuroscientist and tenured Professor in the Department of Neurobiology at the Stanford University School of Medicine. He has made numerous important contributions to the fields of brain development, brain function, and neural plasticity, which is the ability of our nervous system to rewire and learn new behaviors, skills, and cognitive functioning. 
 
Dr. Huberman is a McKnight Foundation and Pew Foundation Fellow and was awarded the Cogan Award in 2017, which is given to the scientist making the largest discoveries in the study of vision. His lab’s most recent work focuses on the influence of vision and respiration on human performance and brain states such as fear and courage. Work from the Huberman Laboratory at Stanford University School of Medicine has been published in top journals including Nature, Science, and Cell and has been featured in TIME, BBC, Scientific American, Discover, and other top media outlets.

In this episode, we dive into: 
 
 - The connection between fear, laziness, and motivation (0:40)
 - The difference between dopamine, adrenaline, and serotonin (13:35)
 - How to increase dopamine (15:04)
 - How to get your mind to stop racing (26:41)

 - What to do if you are having trouble focusing (48:32)
 - Why structure is one of the best ways to create freedom (57:17)
 - How our phones are eroding our creativity, relationships, and more (1:01:37)

title: 6 Techniques to Master Self Discipline | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
Motivation starts things. Discipline finishes them.

This video breaks down why self-discipline is the real driver behind progress — not intensity, not inspiration, and not perfect conditions. Results come from small commitments kept consistently, especially when it’s uncomfortable and inconvenient.

Discipline isn’t punishment. It’s alignment.

What you’ll learn in this video:
-How small commitments compound into real momentum
-Why consistency beats perfection every time
-Using prioritization to stop leaking time and energy
-Turning daily actions into automatic habits
-Delaying short-term comfort for long-term payoff

Discipline is the system that turns intention into execution. When habits are installed, progress no longer depends on mood or motivation. The work gets done because it’s who you are — not because you feel like it.

This video is for anyone who feels stuck, overwhelmed, or inconsistent and wants a clear framework for moving forward without burning out. Progress doesn’t require drastic change — it requires reliable action.

When discipline is in place, success becomes predictable.

This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

These are the only 3 chest exercises you need 😌

An incline press builds your upper pecs, and a flat press is excellent for overall development, especially the middle and lower pecs.

You can hit these in order of priority. You’ll be able to use heavier loads with a flat press, but if your upper chest is lacking, it’ll benefit you to start with that first.

You can complete a chest workout with these two exercises alone, but finishing with chest flys is a great way to bias a weak point and add the extra volume you might need to grow.

2-4 sets of each, depending on your fitness level, and you should be golden! Control the weight, progressive overload, and grow my friends 👊🏻

title: Top Fitness Expert Reveals Best Dumbbell CHEST Workout Techniques
description:
Chest Workout: Building a Stronger Chest 💪🏋️‍♀️

A well-developed chest is a key component of a strong and athletic upper body. The chest muscles, also known as the pectoralis muscles, consist of the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor. 🤸‍♀️

# Chest Muscle Anatomy 🎨
The pectoralis major muscle is divided into two parts: the sternal head (chest muscle) and the clavicular head (upper chest muscle). The pectoralis minor muscle is a smaller muscle that lies underneath the pectoralis major muscle. 💀

# Functions of the Chest Muscles 🤔
The chest muscles have several important functions:

1. _Shoulder Movement_: The chest muscles assist in shoulder movements, such as flexion, extension, and rotation. 🤸‍♀️
2. _Arm Movement_: The chest muscles help to move the arm, particularly in actions such as pushing and throwing. 🏈
3. _Breathing_: The chest muscles also play a role in breathing, particularly during deep inspiration. 👅

# Chest Exercises 🏋️‍♀️
Here are some effective exercises for building a stronger chest:

1. _Bench Press_: This exercise targets the sternal head of the pectoralis major muscle. 🏋️‍♀️
2. _Dumbbell Press_: This exercise targets the sternal head of the pectoralis major muscle. 🏋️‍♀️
3. _Incline Bench Press_: This exercise targets the clavicular head of the pectoralis major muscle. 🏋️‍♀️
4. _Decline Bench Press_: This exercise targets the sternal head of the pectoralis major muscle. 🏋️‍♀️
5. _Chest Fly_: This exercise targets the pectoralis major muscle. 🌈

# Benefits of a Strong Chest 💪
Building a stronger chest can have several benefits:

1. _Improved Athletic Performance_: A strong chest can improve athletic performance in sports that involve pushing, throwing, or lifting. 🏈🏊‍♀️
2. _Increased Strength_: A strong chest can increase overall strength and power. 💪
3. _Better Posture_: A strong chest can help improve posture and reduce the risk of back and shoulder injuries. 🌈
4. _Enhanced Aesthetics_: A well-developed chest can enhance the appearance of the upper body and improve overall muscle balance. 🌟

# Common Chest Injuries 🤕
Here are some common injuries that can affect the chest muscles:

1. _Pectoralis Major Strain_: Overstretching or tearing of the pectoralis major muscle can cause pain and weakness in the chest. 🤕
2. _Pectoralis Minor Strain_: Overstretching or tearing of the pectoralis minor muscle can cause pain and weakness in the chest. 🤕
3. _Costochondritis_: Inflammation of the cartilage that connects the ribs to the breastbone can cause pain and tenderness in the chest. 🤕

# Prevention and Treatment 🏥
To prevent chest injuries, it's essential to:

1. _Warm Up Properly_: Before exercising or engaging in physical activity, warm up your muscles with light cardio and stretching. 🏃‍♀️
2. _Use Proper Form_: When performing exercises, use proper form and technique to avoid putting unnecessary strain on your muscles. 🤓
3. _Stretch Regularly_: Regular stretching can help improve flexibility and reduce muscle tension. 🧘‍♀️

If you do experience a chest injury, it's essential to:

1. _Seek Medical Attention_: If you experience severe pain or swelling, seek medical attention immediately. 🏥
2. _Rest and Ice_: Rest your chest and apply ice to reduce pain and inflammation. ❄️
3. _Stretch and Strengthen_: Once your injury has healed, stretch and strengthen your chest muscles to prevent future injuries. 🏋️‍♀️

title: A complete back workout only requires these key exercises:
description:
A complete back workout only requires these key exercises:

Cable straight-arm pulldown – Primarily targets the lower lats. With arms extended, it minimizes bicep involvement and helps isolate lat engagement.

Seated wide-grip row – Focuses on the middle lats, mid to lower trapezius, and rhomboids, effectively building mid-back thickness.

Wide-grip lat pulldown – Activates the upper to mid lats and teres major, helping to develop the classic V-shaped back.

Cable face pull – Targets the upper traps, rhomboids, and rear delts, enhancing upper back definition and shoulder stability.

title: The PERFECT Back Workout (Sets and Reps Included) #shorts
description:
#shorts #back #backworkout
The perfect back workout should consist of exercises for not just the lats and traps but other important muscles of the back as well.  That said, even that doesn’t make the back workout complete.  In order to round out your back with a well rounded workout you need to fill in the gaps of what is lacking on those popular back exercises and put science back in your training.  That is what we do in this video.

The problem with lat focused training isn’t just that it trains simply a fraction of what the back muscles are capable of but also that many people choose repetitive exercises that work the back in the same plane.  For instance, if you look at the pullup and lat pulldown you will see two major vertical pulling exercises that while not bad to perform in the same back workout, overlook the importance of horizontal pulling if nothing else is done.

It goes beyond this however.  Even when you perform the pullup, many will look at it as a high rep bodyweight exercise only.  They overlook how powerful the movement can be when loaded up with additional weight as in a weighted chin up.  This can become a tremendous compound exercise option and one that is capable of building a lot of back strength, size and overall gains.  Additionally, getting locked in on one grip during this exercise is costing you the chance to work other areas of the back such as the teres major (which in and of itself occupies a large amount of mass above the lats) and therefore limiting the gains you will see from your workout.

Instead, you will want to be sure to mix up chins and pullups along with a foundational strength exercise for the back like the deadlift to start your workout off right.  The deadlift has the ability to work many of the areas of the back all in one shot.  The traps, lats, and lower back all get a heavy dose of overload on this powerhouse of a back exercise.  If you load it heavy enough and refuse to sacrifice your form, this can be an enormous benefit to your overall back development.

We also have an opportunity to introduce some straight arm pushdowns with each warmup set of deadlifts.  This helps to ingrain one of the most important movement patterns you will need to not only perform the deadlift but all next level back exercises.  

As you make your way through the workout however you also don’t want to miss the chance to train explosively.  When you train like an athlete you always want to speed up what you slow down with your heavier weight training. The barbell dead row is a perfect example of this.  Perform this powerful back exercise as a follow up to the deadlift and you will find that even a heavier weight seems lighter and more able to be accelerated.

No perfect back workout would be complete without some additional focused tension towards the lats.  This allows you to develop that mind muscle connection that is important for maximizing hypertrophy of the back.  Choose between one of the two exercises listed and only do one of them.  Just focus on really squeezing each rep and taking the lats through their full range of motion for optimum effect.

Finally, a perfect back workout will not forget the importance of corrective exercises for the back.  Here we want to be sure we work both the lumbar erectors and rotator cuff.  We can do both in one move using the Hyper Y/W combo shown in the video.  You will not need to use heavy weights to do this.  Light weights will still light you up in exactly the way you need to be for best effect.

title: Top 9 Biceps Workouts for Massive Arms | #workout #bicepsworkout
description:
Top 9 Biceps Exercises for Massive Arms 💪

Want bigger, stronger biceps? Check out these 9 killer exercises to sculpt your arms! From barbell curls to Zottman curl, we’ve got the best moves for maximum gains. Perfect for beginners and pros alike. Save this for your next arm day! 🔥

9 Powerfull Biceps Workout:
Here are the top 10 exercises for building biceps, focusing on effectiveness for strength and muscle growth:

1. Barbell Curl - Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, grip a barbell, and curl it up to chest level, keeping elbows tucked. Targets biceps brachii. Do 3-4 sets of 8-12 reps.

2. Dumbbell Curl - Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms up, and curl while keeping elbows close to your body. Allows unilateral work to fix imbalances. 3-4 sets of 10-12 reps per arm.

3. Hammer Curl - Use dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Targets brachialis and brachioradialis alongside biceps. 3-4 sets of 10-12 reps.

4. EZ Bar Curl - Use an EZ bar to reduce wrist strain, curling it up while keeping elbows stationary. Great for isolating biceps. 3-4 sets of 8-12 reps.

5. Concentration Curl - Sit on a bench, rest one arm against your inner thigh, and curl a dumbbell. Maximizes biceps isolation and peak contraction. 3 sets of 12-15 reps per arm.

6. Incline Dumbbell Curl - Lie on an incline bench, curl dumbbells with arms hanging straight down. Stretches biceps for greater range of motion. 3-4 sets of 10-12 reps.

7. Preacher Curl - Use a preacher bench with an EZ bar or dumbbells, curling with arms supported to isolate biceps and prevent swinging. 3-4 sets of 8-12 reps.

8. Cable Curl - Use a cable machine with a straight bar attachment, curling with constant tension on biceps. 3-4 sets of 12-15 reps.

9. Zottman Curl - Curl dumbbells up with palms up, rotate to palms down at the top, and lower slowly. Targets biceps and forearms. 3 sets of 10-12 reps.

Tips: Use proper form to avoid swinging or cheating. Progressively increase weight or reps over time. Rest 60-90 seconds between sets. Combine 2-3 of these in a workout, 1-2 times per week, for optimal biceps growth.

From the cost of training, accessibility, muscle growth, fat loss, progression, and even motivation—this is the ultimate guide to help you decide what actually fits YOUR goals.

What is calisthenics?
Calisthenics uses your own body as resistance: push-ups, pull-ups, dips, squats. And later, advanced skills like the planche, front lever, and muscle-ups. It builds functional strength, mobility, and body control.

What about the gym?
Weight training relies on barbells, dumbbells, and machines. It’s the fastest path to muscle growth, progressive overload, and a physique that looks carved out of stone. Perfect for building size, symmetry, and hitting PRs.

Regular exercise is crucial for maintaining good physical health, especially as women approach their 40s. One of the most significant benefits of exercise is a reduced risk of chronic diseases, such as type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and certain types of cancer. These conditions can be especially prevalent as women age and are more prone to hormonal changes and lifestyle factors that contribute to disease. However, regular exercise has been shown to lower the risk of these conditions by improving blood sugar control, lowering blood pressure, and reducing inflammation.

In addition to reducing the risk of chronic diseases, exercise can improve cardiovascular health, which is essential for maintaining overall well-being. Exercise can strengthen the heart and blood vessels, reduce blood pressure, and improve cholesterol levels, all of which contribute to a healthy cardiovascular system. Improved cardiovascular health can also lead to increased endurance, making it easier for women to perform everyday activities without getting tired quickly.

Another physical benefit of getting fit at 40 is the improvement of muscle strength and bone density. As women age, they are more likely to experience a decline in muscle mass and bone density, which can lead to decreased strength and an increased risk of falls and fractures. However, regular exercise can help prevent or slow down this decline by stimulating muscle growth and strengthening bones.

Mental Benefits:
In addition to the physical benefits, getting fit at 40 can also have a significant impact on mental health. Exercise has been shown to reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression, improve overall mood, and increase cognitive function. These benefits can be particularly important for women as they navigate the challenges of midlife, such as changes in hormonal balance and stressors related to work and family.

Research has shown that exercise can be as effective as medication for treating mild to moderate depression and anxiety. This is because exercise releases endorphins, which are natural mood boosters and can improve overall feelings of well-being. Additionally, exercise can be a way for women to reduce stress and improve their ability to manage stress in their daily lives.

Finally, exercise has been shown to have a positive impact on cognitive function, including memory, attention, and decision-making. This is important for women as they age, as cognitive decline can be a concern. Exercise can help maintain cognitive function and even improve it in some cases.

title: Master the Art of Self Discipline | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
MASTER THE ART OF SELF DISCIPLINE 🧠⚒️

Self-discipline is not talent.
It’s not personality.
It’s not something you’re born with.

It’s a skill.
A decision.
A system you train into yourself.

This video breaks down what real self-discipline actually is — and why it’s the difference between setting goals and living them.

Inside this message, you’ll learn:
• Why discipline outlasts motivation
• How habits replace willpower
• Why follow-through builds identity and self-trust
• How to stop negotiating with yourself
• How to lead your actions even when you don’t feel like it
• Why structure beats intensity every time
• How to act without waiting for the right mood
• How discipline is built quietly, daily, and privately

Self-discipline is the bridge between ambition and results.
Without it, goals stay ideas.
With it, progress becomes inevitable.

This isn’t about perfection.
It’s about consistency.
Doing what you said you would do — especially when it’s uncomfortable, inconvenient, and unseen.

If you’re tired of starting strong and falling off…
If you’re done relying on motivation…
If you’re ready to build habits that don’t ask permission…

This message is for you.

Discipline is not force.
It’s alignment.
And once it’s built, it doesn’t fade.

––––––––––––––––––
This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

title: The Only 13 Minutes You Need To Master Discipline Once And For All | Jocko Willink
description:
The most direct, brutal, and life-changing 13 minutes you’ll hear from Jocko Willink. If you’re tired of excuses, tired of inconsistency, and tired of starting over every Monday - this is for you.

Hit play, turn up the volume, and ask yourself one honest question:
"Am I actually disciplined... or just comfortable?"

This video - Discipline Equals Freedom - is a carefully curated, long-form Jocko Willink experience designed to strip away excuses, kill weakness, and rebuild your mindset around ownership, action, and self-control. No hype. No shortcuts. No motivation tricks. Just discipline, responsibility, and real freedom earned through action.

This video features powerful insights from Jocko Willink’s talks, interviews, and speeches, centered on:
Extreme ownership
Discipline over motivation
Action as the cure for fear
Building freedom through structure
Becoming the person you said you wanted to be

Who is Jocko Willink?

Jocko Willink is a retired U.S. Navy SEAL officer who served for over 20 years and commanded one of the most highly decorated special operations units during the Iraq War. In combat, he learned that success and failure always come down to ownership, discipline, and leadership - not excuses. Those battlefield lessons became the foundation of his life philosophy: if something in your life isn’t working, the responsibility is yours to fix.

After retiring from the military, Jocko became a bestselling author, leadership consultant, and host of the Jocko Podcast, where he teaches people how to apply military-grade discipline to everyday life. His message is simple but demanding: discipline equals freedom. Through structure, consistency, and personal accountability, anyone can build strength, confidence, and control over their life - regardless of their past, circumstances, or emotions.

Follow Jocko:
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/jockowillink/
Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/@JockoPodcastOfficial
Books: Extreme Ownership, Discipline Equals Freedom, and The Dichotomy of Leadership

What you’ll get in this video:
Why discipline equals freedom (and why comfort equals slavery)
Why motivation is unreliable - and discipline is non-negotiable
How excuses quietly destroy your future
Why action eliminates fear instantly
How to stop negotiating with weakness
How to build a disciplined identity - one day at a time

Why watch till the end:
This video is designed to push you into action, not just make you feel inspired for 10 minutes.
Save it. Rewatch it on Sundays and Mondays.
Return to it whenever you feel yourself slipping back into comfort.

This is what real work sounds like.

At one point or another, we’ve all felt stuck in a rut with feelings of laziness and fear. During these times it can be really hard to take a step back and wonder what’s happening in the body, as opposed to just the mind, but it’s the link between the two that can push us through it.  

Neurotransmitters have some incredible power over how we function. Dopamine is responsible for craving, motivation, and pursuit. Adrenaline relates to agitation and endurance. Serotonin helps us be grateful and feel good about what we have. And acetylcholine can help us focus. This is just a snapshot of the chemical symphony happening in our bodies all the time, and we can actually leverage these inner reactions to better understand the way we react to the world around us and make positive changes. 

Today on The Dhru Purohit Podcast, Dhru talks to Dr. Andrew Huberman about opening the window into our neurochemistry, training the nervous system, and confronting our inner real estate. 

Dr. Andrew Huberman is a neuroscientist and tenured Professor in the Department of Neurobiology at the Stanford University School of Medicine. He has made numerous important contributions to the fields of brain development, brain function, and neural plasticity, which is the ability of our nervous system to rewire and learn new behaviors, skills, and cognitive functioning. 
 
Dr. Huberman is a McKnight Foundation and Pew Foundation Fellow and was awarded the Cogan Award in 2017, which is given to the scientist making the largest discoveries in the study of vision. His lab’s most recent work focuses on the influence of vision and respiration on human performance and brain states such as fear and courage. Work from the Huberman Laboratory at Stanford University School of Medicine has been published in top journals including Nature, Science, and Cell and has been featured in TIME, BBC, Scientific American, Discover, and other top media outlets.

title: 6 Techniques to Master Self Discipline | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
Motivation starts things. Discipline finishes them.

This video breaks down why self-discipline is the real driver behind progress — not intensity, not inspiration, and not perfect conditions. Results come from small commitments kept consistently, especially when it’s uncomfortable and inconvenient.

Discipline isn’t punishment. It’s alignment.

What you’ll learn in this video:
-How small commitments compound into real momentum
-Why consistency beats perfection every time
-Using prioritization to stop leaking time and energy
-Turning daily actions into automatic habits
-Delaying short-term comfort for long-term payoff

Discipline is the system that turns intention into execution. When habits are installed, progress no longer depends on mood or motivation. The work gets done because it’s who you are — not because you feel like it.

This video is for anyone who feels stuck, overwhelmed, or inconsistent and wants a clear framework for moving forward without burning out. Progress doesn’t require drastic change — it requires reliable action.

When discipline is in place, success becomes predictable.

This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

Neurotransmitters have some incredible power over how we function. Dopamine is responsible for craving, motivation, and pursuit. Adrenaline relates to agitation and endurance. Serotonin helps us be grateful and feel good about what we have. And acetylcholine can help us focus. This is just a snapshot of the chemical symphony happening in our bodies all the time, and we can actually leverage these inner reactions to better understand the way we react to the world around us and make positive changes.

Dr. Andrew Huberman is a neuroscientist and tenured Professor in the Department of Neurobiology at the Stanford University School of Medicine. He has made numerous important contributions to the fields of brain development, brain function, and neural plasticity, which is the ability of our nervous system to rewire and learn new behaviors, skills, and cognitive functioning. 
 
Dr. Huberman is a McKnight Foundation and Pew Foundation Fellow and was awarded the Cogan Award in 2017, which is given to the scientist making the largest discoveries in the study of vision. His lab’s most recent work focuses on the influence of vision and respiration on human performance and brain states such as fear and courage. Work from the Huberman Laboratory at Stanford University School of Medicine has been published in top journals including Nature, Science, and Cell and has been featured in TIME, BBC, Scientific American, Discover, and other top media outlets.

title: The Science of Making & Breaking Habits
description:
In this episode, I review the science of habit formation and habit elimination and how the process of neuroplasticity (brain rewiring) underlies these processes. 

I describe two new systems for habit formation. The first system is grounded in the neuroscience of brain states and our ability to perform (and to avoid) certain tasks at different phases of the 24-hour day. The second system focuses on 21-day habit formation and consolidation.

I also discuss "task bracketing" as an approach to enhancing habit formation and eliminating unwanted habits and the neural circuits that underlie task bracketing in the basal ganglia (a brain region for generating and stopping behaviors). I also review the science of dopamine rewards and how to apply that knowledge to shaping habits. 

The science and tools in this episode ought to be helpful for anyone looking to build better habits and eliminate unwanted habits for school, work, fitness, relationships, creative endeavors, and more—indeed for any person or situation where behavioral changes are needed.

title: 1 Minute a Day - Build Discipline
description:
I get some messages that go something like "I want to improve my life, but I don't have the motivation to do anything. Not even something like drinking more water."

I get a surprising amount of these messages.

Yes, sometimes this is because something is awry in our diet, sleep, lifestyle, etc. 

However, sometimes we're just lacking discipline.

We can't always rely on motivation. We don't wait for inspiration to brush our teeth. We just do it.

SOME discipline is required to do almost anything in life.

Going to failure seems to be good at building discipline. Pushing yourself beyond the point of "ugh I want to give up" seems to help.

I give a simple exercise here that's been used by martial artists for millennia to build strength and discipline.

It doesn't HAVE to be this. You can apply the failure/discipline principle to any exercise. But this one works well because it's relatively safe and training our legs can really suck.

In this case, that's a good thing.

title: 6 Techniques to Master Self Discipline | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
Motivation starts things. Discipline finishes them.

This video breaks down why self-discipline is the real driver behind progress — not intensity, not inspiration, and not perfect conditions. Results come from small commitments kept consistently, especially when it’s uncomfortable and inconvenient.

Discipline isn’t punishment. It’s alignment.

What you’ll learn in this video:
-How small commitments compound into real momentum
-Why consistency beats perfection every time
-Using prioritization to stop leaking time and energy
-Turning daily actions into automatic habits
-Delaying short-term comfort for long-term payoff

Discipline is the system that turns intention into execution. When habits are installed, progress no longer depends on mood or motivation. The work gets done because it’s who you are — not because you feel like it.

This video is for anyone who feels stuck, overwhelmed, or inconsistent and wants a clear framework for moving forward without burning out. Progress doesn’t require drastic change — it requires reliable action.

When discipline is in place, success becomes predictable.

This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

title: 1 Minute a Day - Build Discipline
description:
I get some messages that go something like "I want to improve my life, but I don't have the motivation to do anything. Not even something like drinking more water."

I get a surprising amount of these messages.

Yes, sometimes this is because something is awry in our diet, sleep, lifestyle, etc. 

However, sometimes we're just lacking discipline.

We can't always rely on motivation. We don't wait for inspiration to brush our teeth. We just do it.

SOME discipline is required to do almost anything in life.

Going to failure seems to be good at building discipline. Pushing yourself beyond the point of "ugh I want to give up" seems to help.

I give a simple exercise here that's been used by martial artists for millennia to build strength and discipline.

It doesn't HAVE to be this. You can apply the failure/discipline principle to any exercise. But this one works well because it's relatively safe and training our legs can really suck.

In this case, that's a good thing.

At one point or another, we’ve all felt stuck in a rut with feelings of laziness and fear. During these times it can be really hard to take a step back and wonder what’s happening in the body, as opposed to just the mind, but it’s the link between the two that can push us through it.  

Neurotransmitters have some incredible power over how we function. Dopamine is responsible for craving, motivation, and pursuit. Adrenaline relates to agitation and endurance. Serotonin helps us be grateful and feel good about what we have. And acetylcholine can help us focus. This is just a snapshot of the chemical symphony happening in our bodies all the time, and we can actually leverage these inner reactions to better understand the way we react to the world around us and make positive changes. 

Today on The Dhru Purohit Podcast, Dhru talks to Dr. Andrew Huberman about opening the window into our neurochemistry, training the nervous system, and confronting our inner real estate. 

Dr. Andrew Huberman is a neuroscientist and tenured Professor in the Department of Neurobiology at the Stanford University School of Medicine. He has made numerous important contributions to the fields of brain development, brain function, and neural plasticity, which is the ability of our nervous system to rewire and learn new behaviors, skills, and cognitive functioning. 
 
Dr. Huberman is a McKnight Foundation and Pew Foundation Fellow and was awarded the Cogan Award in 2017, which is given to the scientist making the largest discoveries in the study of vision. His lab’s most recent work focuses on the influence of vision and respiration on human performance and brain states such as fear and courage. Work from the Huberman Laboratory at Stanford University School of Medicine has been published in top journals including Nature, Science, and Cell and has been featured in TIME, BBC, Scientific American, Discover, and other top media outlets.

title: How To Master Your Time
description:
Vusi Thembekwayo talks about time management.

Time is the most precious resource you have. It’s the one thing you can’t get back. So if you want to be a successful business person, you need to master your time

Here are a few reasons why time management is so important for business:

It helps you achieve your goals faster. When you have a clear plan and you know how to prioritize your tasks, you can get more done in less time. This frees up your time to focus on the most important things, and it helps you reach your goals sooner.

It reduces stress. When you feel like you’re constantly running behind and you’re never able to get everything done, it can be very stressful. Time management can help you feel more in control of your time and your workload, which can lead to a significant reduction in stress levels.

It improves your decision-making. When you have a clear understanding of your priorities and you’re able to make decisions quickly, you’re more likely to make good decisions. This is important for business people, as they often have to make quick decisions that can have a big impact on the company.

It helps you build better relationships. When you’re able to manage your time effectively, you’re more likely to be able to meet deadlines and deliver on promises. This can help you build trust and credibility with your clients and colleagues, which can lead to better relationships.

title: The SEVEN Things You NEED To Learn for Your Financial FREEDOM - Robert Kiyosaki
description:
When Robert Kiyosaki was young, his poor dad always told him the best path to success was to go to school. This was and still is advice spread to young people around the globe. 

The problem is, what does school teach you about money? Nothing! 

Robert’s rich dad, on the other hand, didn’t have a college degree. He had to drop out of school in order to help run his family business, which started as a local store. Yet he was very rich and successful, eventually building a real estate empire complete with a hotel on the beach. 

The idea that school will make you a success is perpetrated everywhere and all the time. What will make you rich is not going to school and learning book smarts but rather gaining financial smarts—learning how money works and how to make it work for you.

You need to learn to speak the language of money to be successful. That takes financial education, which opens up a whole new world, a world where you can succeed on your own terms. Unfortunately, our schools don’t teach that language. They teach you the basics, and then they either teach you a specific trade or skill, or they simply train you to be an employee.

Watch and find out the seven things they don’t teach you in school, but that are imperative to financial freedom.

title: Mastering the Art of Daily Excellence | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
Success is not complicated.
But it does demand something most people are unwilling to give.

This video breaks down the real reason most people never succeed — and it has nothing to do with talent, luck, or opportunity.

🚀 Success comes down to work.
Every single day.
No shortcuts. No secrets. No motivation required.

In this talk, you’ll learn:
🔥 Why motivation is unreliable and discipline is everything
🔥 Why most people quit right before momentum kicks in
🔥 The real difference between hard work and consistent work
🔥 Why discomfort is the price of progress
🔥 How discipline beats talent every time
🔥 Why success is built in silence long before results appear
🔥 How to keep working when nothing seems to be happening

Most people wait to feel ready.
Most people wait for motivation.
Most people wait for things to get easier.

And that’s why most people stay average.

This video is a wake-up call for anyone tired of talking about success and ready to live it. If you’re willing to work when you’re tired, push when it’s uncomfortable, and stay disciplined when results are delayed — this message is for you.

⚠️ This is not about hype.
⚠️ This is not about shortcuts.
⚠️ This is about standards, discipline, and daily execution.

If you’re ready to stop waiting and start working, press play.

—

Most people never reach their potential for one simple reason:

💥 Doing what’s hard isn’t punishment.
💥 It’s training.
💥 It’s how identity is forged.

In this message, you’ll learn:
• Why the easy path produces weak results
• How discomfort builds discipline, grit, and resilience
• Why confidence is earned through repetition, not hype
• How doing hard things rewires your nervous system for pressure
• Why leaders are built in private, not in public moments
• How consistency under strain creates unstoppable momentum

🔥 This isn’t about motivation.
🔥 It’s about standards.
🔥 It’s about becoming the kind of person who doesn’t flinch under pressure.

If you’re tired of comfort holding you back…
If you’re ready to stop negotiating with your limits…
If you want strength that doesn’t disappear when things get hard…

Watch this carefully. Then choose one hard thing today — and do it.

Because the hard path doesn’t just change what you achieve.
It changes who you become.

title: Wake Up & Work Hard The Secret to Unstoppable Success | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
There’s an invisible line in your life.
Everything you accept, tolerate, and settle for exists beneath it.

That line is your standard.

This video breaks down why real change doesn’t come from motivation, goals, or hype — it comes from raising what you demand from yourself. Not occasionally. Consistently.

If you’ve ever wondered why:
• You make progress, then slide back
• Habits don’t stick
• The same problems keep repeating
• Breakthroughs never last

The answer is almost always the same:
Your standards haven’t changed.

🔥 In this talk, you’ll learn:
• Why you don’t get what you want — you get what you tolerate
• How standards quietly shape habits, identity, and results
• The difference between raising the ceiling vs raising the floor
• Why motivation fades but standards hold
• How identity locks in progress (or sabotages it)
• Why people succeed temporarily — then collapse
• How to upgrade your internal “thermostat”
• What it actually takes to make change permanent

This isn’t about pushing harder.
It’s about refusing to live below a level you’ve outgrown.

When your standard changes:
• Discipline becomes automatic
• Excuses stop fitting
• Consistency becomes normal
• Results stabilize instead of disappearing

You don’t need more information.
You don’t need the perfect plan.
You need a higher standard.

And once that standard is set, your life has no choice but to rise to meet it. 🚀

This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

title: 3 Methods to Develop a Millionaire Mindset | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
Wealth starts long before money shows up. It starts in how you think, what you tolerate, and what you do every day when no one is watching.

This video breaks down the mindset behind long-term success — not as a fantasy, but as a discipline. It focuses on how beliefs shape behavior, how habits compound, and why growth must be intentional if you want results that last.

A “millionaire mindset” isn’t about income. It’s about identity.

What this video covers:
-Rewriting limiting beliefs around money and success
-Using discipline to turn goals into progress
-Building habits that support long-term growth
-Adopting continuous learning as a lifestyle
-Designing your environment and influences for success
-Practicing gratitude as a stabilizer, not a slogan

Success isn’t something you chase. It’s something you become aligned with through consistent action. When beliefs change, behavior follows. When behavior stabilizes, results appear.

This video is for anyone serious about upgrading how they think, work, and live — not overnight, but permanently.

This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

Hello friends welcome to inspire story hub youtube channel

In this video-
This story is about the remarkable transformation of a beggar who lived at a railway station and survived by asking for alms. One day, he encountered a well-dressed man who told him that to receive something in life, one must also give. The beggar reflected deeply on this idea and decided to start offering flowers in exchange for alms. This simple act of giving made him stand out, and people began appreciating his gesture. As a result, he started receiving more alms, which he used to buy flowers and gradually turned his small act into a business. Over time, he transitioned from being a beggar to becoming a successful flower merchant. This transformation happened because he changed his perspective and recognized his own worth. The story highlights the power of self-respect and a positive mindset, showing that when we stop seeing ourselves as small and dare to think big, we can achieve great success.

title: How to Become Successful in Life | Hindi Motivational Story
description:
How to Become Successful in Life | Hindi Motivational Story 


In this deeply inspiring Hindi motivational story, we follow the journey of a young boy named Rahul, who spends his summer holidays with his wise and loving Nanaji. Curious about life, Rahul asks a question many of us struggle with —
“Nanaji, how do I become a successful person?”

But instead of a direct answer, his grandfather gives him a life experience. Through two plants — one grown in comfort and one grown in adversity — Rahul learns a profound life lesson that success doesn’t come from avoiding problems, but from facing challenges, growing stronger, and embracing the struggle.

This is not just a story — it’s a powerful message for anyone who feels stuck, afraid of failure, or unsure about how to move forward in life.
If you’re a student, dreamer, or someone going through tough times — this story will inspire you to keep going.

📖 What You’ll Learn from This Story:
 • Why struggles are necessary for real success
 • How comfort can limit your growth
 • The difference between surviving and thriving
 • The value of resilience, strength, and deep roots in life
 • How to turn your pain into power

💡 Moral of the Story:
True success is not born from comfort, but from courage. Just like the tree that grew stronger through storms, we too must face life’s challenges to reach our full potential. Comfort zones create safety, but not greatness.

title: Never Settle for Mediocrity - David Goggins Motivation
description:
Mediocrity is comfortable. It’s easy. It’s what most people choose. But not you. If you’re here, it means something inside of you refuses to accept average. In this powerful message, David Goggins reminds us why settling is the slow death of potential—and why you must rise above it every single day.

We live in a world that encourages comfort and quick wins, but true fulfillment only comes through discipline, pain, and the pursuit of something greater. Goggins speaks from experience—he’s been at the bottom, faced every excuse, every setback, and every voice telling him to stop. But he didn’t settle. He chose to become more.

To never settle for mediocrity means doing the things most people avoid. It means waking up early, pushing through fatigue, training your mind, and staying committed when no one’s watching. It means demanding more of yourself, not just once, but constantly. And it means being willing to suffer for growth, to embrace discomfort, and to keep going when it gets hard.

If you feel like giving in, remember this: greatness isn’t found in talent, or luck, or comfort. It’s found in the quiet moments when you push through the pain, when you refuse to quit, and when you choose to fight for a better version of yourself—even when no one else understands it.

Mediocrity will always be there, ready to welcome you back. But once you taste discipline, purpose, and power—you’ll never want to go back. Choose greatness. Stay hard.

title: The Science of Setting & Achieving Goals
description:
In this episode, I discuss the science of setting, assessing, and pursuing goals. I explain the neural (brain) circuits that underlie goal setting and pursuit. Then I describe nine science-supported tools anyone can apply toward their goals. I explain when and how to use goal visualization, when to use multitasking and how to use specific rewards to improve the likelihood of reaching your goals. I also explain why envisioning failures and their consequences are effective and how to set goals of the appropriate level of challenge. I also explain how the molecule dopamine is used to gauge our progress toward milestones and long-term overarching goals and how to leverage dopamine for goal pursuit. Finally, I explain a unique tool called 'space-time bridging' that can be used to support all aspects of goal setting, assessment, and pursuit. This episode ought to be useful for anyone seeking to improve their performance in work, school, exercise, athletics, or personal development.

title: Transform Your Life With This 6 Month Success Plan | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
Six months can change everything — if you use them correctly.

This video explains how a short, focused window of disciplined execution can completely reshape your life. Not through luck, hype, or burnout — but through clarity, consistency, and the ruthless elimination of distractions. When effort is intentional and sustained, progress accelerates fast.

Momentum is built, not wished for.

Here’s what gets broken down:
⏱️ Why six months of focused effort can outperform years of scattered work
⏱️ Eliminating distractions to protect momentum
⏱️ Why execution always beats motivation
⏱️ Setting clear, measurable targets that force action
⏱️ Building discipline and mental toughness that holds under pressure

Most people don’t fail because they lack ability. They fail because they hesitate, negotiate with themselves, and let distractions dilute effort. This video shows why a committed six-month push — with structure and standards — is enough to create visible, irreversible progress.

This is for anyone who feels stuck, impatient with slow results, or tired of restarting. You don’t need more time. You need better focus and firmer execution.

Work with precision.
Stay consistent.
Let momentum do the rest.

This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

A sheep never leads. A lion never follows.

Mental strength is the ability to keep going even when things are tough, to find creative solutions to problems, and to stay positive and focused even when things are against you.

When it comes to developing mental toughness and strength, it is important to set yourself up for success by having a positive mindset. 

No one is immune to challenges, pain, or grief and we all need to find ways to deal with these things in a healthy way.

Mental toughness is a quality that everyone can benefit from, whether you’re trying to lose weight, to earn money or simply improve your outlook on life.

No one ever said that becoming mentally tough would be easy. You will inevitably face setbacks along the way. 
Don’t let these get you down; instead, use them as motivation to keep going.
Because, In life every setback is an opportunity to learn and grow.

Mental toughness is not something that you’re born with. It’s something that you have to work for. 

In this video, I share 9 strategies for how to be mentally strong. These are things that I have personally used to overcome challenges in my own life, and I know they will work for you, too.
Watch the video and start implementing these strategies today to become mentally strong!

---------------------------------------

The ability to bend without breaking.
To endure without collapsing.
To grow stronger under weight instead of being crushed by it.

title: How To Build Unstoppable Confidence | Jim Rohn Motivation

Confidence is not something you’re born with. It’s something you build — deliberately.

Rather than chasing motivation, this talk focuses on the mechanics of self-belief: how consistency creates trust, how fear becomes training, and how learning only matters when it’s applied.

Key ideas covered:
-How confidence is built step by step
-Why discipline and consistency create self-trust
-Using fear as a tool instead of avoiding it
-The role of self-education and applied knowledge
-Why your environment and associations matter

Confidence doesn’t come from big moments. It comes from daily decisions that prove to you — repeatedly — that you can handle what life puts in front of you. Every kept commitment strengthens it. Every avoided challenge weakens it.

This video is for anyone tired of self-doubt and ready to build confidence the only way it lasts: through action, discipline, and personal responsibility.

title: Powerful Positive Affirmations For Success | Positive Morning Affirmations | Positive Thinking
description:
Good Morning! Today, I want to talk about the power of positive affirmations for success. We all have goals and dreams that we want to achieve, but sometimes we get caught up in negative thoughts and self-doubt. That's where positive affirmations come in.

Positive affirmations are powerful statements that can help reprogram our minds and shift our mindset towards success. By repeating these affirmations daily, we can train our brains to think positively and attract success into our lives.

So, I want to share with you some powerful positive morning affirmations that you can start your day with. These affirmations will help you set the tone for a positive and successful day ahead.

1. I am capable of achieving anything I set my mind to.
2. I am confident and believe in my abilities.
3. I am surrounded by love and support.
4. I am grateful for all the opportunities that come my way.
5. I am worthy of success and happiness.
6. I am in control of my thoughts and emotions.
7. I am resilient and can overcome any challenges.
8. I am constantly growing and learning.
9. I am focused and determined to reach my goals.
10. I am creating a life of abundance and prosperity.

Remember, our thoughts become our reality. So, by starting your day with these positive affirmations, you are setting yourself up for success and a positive mindset.

But it's not just about saying these affirmations, it's about truly believing in them and taking action towards your goals. Positive thinking alone won't bring success, but it will help you stay motivated and focused on your journey.

So, let's make a commitment to ourselves to incorporate these positive affirmations into our daily routine. Let's choose to think positively and attract success into our lives.

I hope these affirmations will inspire and empower you to reach for your dreams and achieve success. Remember, you are capable and deserving of all the success in the world. Believe in yourself and keep moving forward. Have a positive and successful day ahead!

title: How To Build Unstoppable Confidence | Jim Rohn Motivation
description:
Confidence is not something you’re born with. It’s something you build — deliberately.

This video breaks down how real confidence is formed over time, not through hype or validation, but through discipline, repetition, and proof you give yourself. Confidence grows when you keep small promises, face discomfort, and develop the ability to rely on your own actions under pressure.

Rather than chasing motivation, this talk focuses on the mechanics of self-belief: how consistency creates trust, how fear becomes training, and how learning only matters when it’s applied.

Key ideas covered:
-How confidence is built step by step
-Why discipline and consistency create self-trust
-Using fear as a tool instead of avoiding it
-The role of self-education and applied knowledge
-Why your environment and associations matter

Confidence doesn’t come from big moments. It comes from daily decisions that prove to you — repeatedly — that you can handle what life puts in front of you. Every kept commitment strengthens it. Every avoided challenge weakens it.

This video is for anyone tired of self-doubt and ready to build confidence the only way it lasts: through action, discipline, and personal responsibility.

This transcript and video were written & produced by Dus Rawling, inspired by the ideas and philosophies of Jim Rohn.

title: David Goggins is INSANE!
description:
David Goggins is widely regarded as one of the most inspirational figures in the world of personal development, endurance athletics, and mental toughness. His life story is a powerful example of resilience, determination, and the ability to completely transform oneself despite extreme adversity. He is a retired Navy SEAL, an ultra-endurance athlete, a former Air Force Tactical Air Control Party member, and a motivational speaker who has built a reputation for pushing the limits of human performance. What sets him apart is not simply his accomplishments, but the journey of hardship and transformation that forged his mindset and philosophy.

Goggins was born in 1975 in Buffalo, New York, into a difficult and traumatic childhood. His father was abusive, and the environment in which he was raised was filled with violence and instability. As a young boy, Goggins struggled academically, battled racism, and endured a household environment that was mentally and physically damaging. He also suffered from a learning disability, which made his time in school even more challenging. His early years gave him a sense of fear, insecurity, and lack of self-worth that stayed with him well into his young adulthood. At one point, he was overweight, unmotivated, and living a life that he himself described as unfulfilled and purposeless.

The turning point in his life came when he made the decision to join the United States military. At first, he joined the Air Force and served as part of the Tactical Air Control Party, but later he pursued the much more difficult path of becoming a Navy SEAL. His journey toward earning the SEAL trident was one of the most grueling aspects of his life. He failed to qualify multiple times due to injuries and setbacks, but his determination and refusal to quit ultimately carried him through. He went through the infamous Basic Underwater Demolition SEAL training, better known as BUD/S, three times before graduating. This period of his life became the foundation of the mental toughness principles he would later teach to millions.

As a Navy SEAL, Goggins served in combat zones and built his reputation as someone who embraced suffering and hardship as opportunities to grow. However, his challenges did not stop after his military career. He went on to pursue ultra-endurance athletics, which includes ultramarathons, long-distance cycling, and other extreme events that test physical and mental capacity. Despite being diagnosed with a heart condition early in his endurance career, he went on to complete some of the most brutal races in the world, including the Badwater 135 ultramarathon across Death Valley, Ironman triathlons, and countless other endurance challenges. He frequently competed with broken bones, torn muscles, or other injuries, but continued anyway, motivated by his mindset of never giving up.

What makes Goggins unique is not only his ability to endure extreme conditions but also his philosophy about suffering and personal growth. He developed the concept of the “cookie jar,” which is the practice of drawing strength from past victories and hardships whenever facing new challenges. He also emphasizes the “forty percent rule,” which suggests that when the human mind believes it has reached its limit, it is often only operating at about forty percent of its true capacity. Through discipline, grit, and self-mastery, he believes anyone can unlock hidden reserves of strength and resilience.

Goggins became widely known outside of the military and endurance community through his bestselling memoir “Can’t Hurt Me.” The book details his life story, his philosophy of accountability, and his approach to overcoming mental barriers. It resonated with millions around the world who were inspired by his honesty, rawness, and refusal to sugarcoat the realities of hardship. In the book, he introduced concepts like the accountability mirror, which involves confronting oneself with brutal honesty in order to make real change.

Beyond the book, Goggins has become a highly sought-after motivational speaker. He has spoken to Fortune 500 companies, sports teams, and individuals across the globe, sharing his philosophy of discipline, suffering, and resilience. His message often revolves around the idea that growth comes from discomfort and that most people live far below their potential because they avoid pain and challenges. Instead of seeking comfort, Goggins teaches that embracing hardship can forge an indomitable spirit and lead to extraordinary achievements.

Physical Fitness vs. Mental Fortitude: Which Matters More?
— @chriswillx @piersmorgan

Chris Williamson believes that physical strength is the base from which mental strength grows. He explains that most people today are lacking in both areas, but physical action is the quickest way to improve mental health. Activities like walking or going to the gym can shift mood and focus more effectively than simply thinking about problems. For Williamson, consistent physical practice helps build the foundation needed for a stronger mind.

Piers Morgan, however, puts mental strength first. He argues that young people focus heavily on physical appearance and gym routines but are often mentally fragile. Morgan sees mental resilience as the key issue facing today’s generation. While Williamson acknowledges this point, he maintains that the path to mental toughness starts with the body, not the mind.

title: Growth Mindset vs Fixed Mindset | Vusi Thembekwayo
description:
Vusi Thembekwayo talking about growth mindset.

Embracing the Growth Mindset

In the vast tapestry of life, we hold the threads of endless possibilities. It’s not just about where we stand today, but how far we can stretch our wings, expand our horizons, and evolve into the best versions of ourselves. Welcome to the realm of the growth mindset, a transformative perspective that fuels our journey of self-discovery, resilience, and achievement.

Imagine a mindset that sees challenges as opportunities, setbacks as stepping stones, and failures as invaluable lessons. A growth mindset embraces the belief that our abilities and intelligence are not fixed but can be nurtured, developed, and honed with effort, perseverance, and an unwavering commitment to personal growth.

It’s about recognizing that true success lies not solely in the destination but in the journey itself—the relentless pursuit of improvement, the determination to push boundaries, and the audacity to dream big. With a growth mindset, we step out of our comfort zones, embrace discomfort as a catalyst for growth, and unlock our boundless potential.

This mindset beckons us to be architects of our own destiny, where challenges become opportunities to learn, adapt, and thrive. It’s a mindset that celebrates progress over perfection, understanding that every step forward, no matter how small, is a triumph that propels us closer to our goals.

But the growth mindset is not just about personal growth—it’s about fostering a culture of empowerment, collaboration, and continuous improvement. It’s about supporting and lifting others as we rise, for we understand that when one person grows, we all do.
